title: Expansion of effective pore size on hydrogen physisorption of porous carbons at low temperatures with high pressures
material_description: CS-C | coconut-shell carbon (CS-C): carbonized at 900 °C, 1 h, N2, ball-milled; no silica elimination, no activation; contains residual silica phytoliths
source_location: main-5 (journal p. 368), Fig. 5(a), QExcess at 77 K up to 1 bar, series CS-C (black markers), digitized marker
notes: archive: f5a_CS-C.json (point index 0); Fig. 5(a), Fig. 5(b) and Fig. S2 curves are coded as separate runs (each plotted curve one run); the paper does not say whether 5(a) is the low-pressure part of the 5(b) run, and the S2 QTotal curve is computed from the QExcess data; isotherm_point_count is a lower bound: markers that could be identified; further low-pressure markers overlap other markers or series and could not be counted; sample CS-C: SSA is the NLDFT specific surface area of Table 1 (footnote a), stored in bet_surface_area_m2_g with surface_area_method DFT; V<4nm (NLDFT) 0.120 cm3/g (no schema field); V2-50nm stored as mesopore volume; EDS (Fig. 2f, at%): C 85.64, O 12.19, Si 2.16 (residual silica); degassing 473 K (printed) for 12 h under vacuum; H2 99.999%; instrument BEL-HP (BEL Japan), volumetric
basis_evidence: "The gas adsorption including H2, can usually be described by two parameters: the total adsorption, QTotal, and the excess adsorption, QExcess. ... The QExcess determined from the experimentally measured adsorption is the amount of gas adsorbed onto the adsorbent surface [50]. The QTotal refers to the sum of QExcess and the amounts of bulk gas compressed in the pores." Eq. (11): QExcess = QTotal - VPore*rho_bulk(P,T). Table 1 reports QExcess and QTotal side by side at 77 K and 60 bar (p. 367-368).
